entries.claim: The stand-in skill edit replaces only the fixed line at SKILL.md:412 and forbids changing any other line. That leaves the bullet's lead-in at SKILL.md:406-410 ('End your message with exactly these words, on a line of their own, with nothing after them. This is the later-release line:') and the code fence still wrapping the new text, so the instruction to start seldon:readiness lands as a verbatim line to print, inside a fence. The 'end with the agent's reply' clause then contradicts the lead-in, and 'that tool' has no antecedent anywhere in the SKILL.md body.
entries.failure_scenario: An executor follows lines 72-74 literally and changes only line 412. In run 1, the bare /seldon reaches the all-four-documents bullet and is told to end its message with 'exactly these words', which are now the fenced instruction text. The model can print that text, or a confused mix of it, and never call the agent tool. The Outcome rule at PLAN-1.md:93 then reads this as 'run 1 never started the agent', which is the Not scoped / not shown stop under D-02 and D-04 d. D-04 a caps the probe at two runs and the plan has no retry, so the phase halts on a defect in the stand-in, not on how the host behaves, and Daneel gets a misattributed result. The fix belongs in the plan: replace the whole bullet body from 'write nothing. End your message...' through the closing fence, and name the tool in the instruction.

entries.claim: The crossing rule in Task 1 says an epic crosses when its Requirements line holds IDs from 'two or more' PRD `### ` categories. The fixed crossing form in Context has room for exactly two, `(<category> and <category>)`, and no form is given for three or more, so the agent has no fixed line for a case its own rule defines.
entries.failure_scenario: An epics.md, hand-edited or seeded, has an epic carrying up to 5 IDs that span three categories, e.g. CAT-01, LOAN-01 and a third category's ID, with no Kind: boundaries decision. The agent must report the crossing but has no fixed form for it, so it improvises, e.g. '(Catalog, Loans and Billing)' or '(Catalog and Loans and Billing)'. Under D-20 the skill treats a reply outside D-08's fixed forms as a check that did not run. A design with a real finding then gets the did-not-run and not-checked lines in place of the report, or a byte-for-byte grader in Plan 3/5 fails. One fix is to say the form lists every category, joined in one stated way, or to cap the rule at two.

entries.claim: `says-no-findings` (and `asks-nothing`) grade `last_message`, but Tasks 1 and 2 tell the skill to say the no-findings line and only then run the handoff's Glob for `.planning/PROJECT.md`. `last_message` holds only the text after the last tool result, so a run that does exactly what the plan says fails the grader.
entries.failure_scenario: In the kept phase 7 trace evals/results/phase-7-traces/stale-prd-trace.jsonl, the stale line was said before a tool call, and the result (the grader's `last_message`) starts at the text after the last tool call. That is why phase 7 graded such lines with `target: trace` (evals/stale-prd/graders/says-stale-line.md). Here the order in Task 1 line 78 ("say the no-findings line, ask nothing, and give the handoff") and Task 2 line 101 (Glob for PROJECT.md inside the handoff) produces: agent result -> text "The readiness check found nothing to fix." -> Glob .planning/PROJECT.md -> text "To hand this design to Cadence, run:" plus the command. `last_message` then lacks the no-findings line, `says-no-findings` scores 0, and resume-later misses 1.00 on correct behavior. The plan's three-try retry budget then goes on a grader and order problem the plan itself created. For the same reason, `asks-nothing` only sees the text after the Glob, so a question asked before it passes. The fix is to pin the order in the skill text (Glob for PROJECT.md before any report text) or to grade the line on the trace.

entries.claim: Task 4 adds D-10's exception (the finding lines are the rerun's change) only to the "The spine rerun" and "The epics rerun" paragraphs. The absolute rules at HEAD in section 15 ("carry nothing from the conversation into the spine", SKILL.md:1021-1023; "The one thing it takes from the conversation is the user's answers to this step's own questions", SKILL.md:1014-1016) and section 18 ("never the earlier conversation, whatever it holds", SKILL.md:1298) stay unchanged and contradict it. Task 4's Reads don't list either section.
entries.failure_scenario: On `/seldon fix them` after a report whose only finding is E-02's crossing, the model goes to "The spine rerun", which defers to "The spine step" (SKILL.md:1144, 1016-1017). There section 15 still says to carry nothing from the conversation into the spine, with no exception named. A model that follows that rule rebuilds the spine from the files alone, so no boundary is added. The stamp is already current, so no Edit is needed, and AC3's "edits spine.md" fails. This is the outcome D-10 rejects: a rerun with no finding carried, so the same finding returns. D-10 calls this "this phase's one named exception", but the exception is never named where the absolute rule lives.

entries.claim: Task 1 Verify (2) counts `seldon:readiness` in SKILL.md and says "Each prints 0 today". Plan 3 depends on Plan 2, whose Task 2 already puts the scoped entry naming `seldon:readiness` in SKILL.md's allowed-tools, so this sub-check cannot fail.
entries.failure_scenario: After Plan 2, `grep -cF 'seldon:readiness' skills/seldon/SKILL.md` prints 1 from the frontmatter grant alone. An executor who never writes the start instruction ("start exactly one agent, `seldon:readiness`") into the new section 22 still passes Verify (2) for that item. Only Task 3's live run would catch the gap, after a retry is spent.

entries.claim: Task 1 puts `samples/readiness/prd.md` in a folder with no `brief.md` and adds no `ELSEWHERE` entry for it. The stamp test in tests/samples.test.mjs therefore reports it as `stamped, but no parent found`, so Task 1 Verify (2), Task 2 Verify (2) and the third must-be-true all fail as written. Task 1's Files list leaves out tests/samples.test.mjs, even though Task 1 names it as a Pin. Task 2 adds only the `readiness-uncovered/epics.md` entry.
entries.failure_scenario: `stampProblems()` (tests/samples.test.mjs lines 27-39) walks samples/ recursively. For `readiness/prd.md` it sets `sibling = readiness/brief.md`. Task 1 creates only prd.md, spine.md and epics.md in that folder, so `existsSync` is false and it falls back to `ELSEWHERE['readiness/prd.md']`. That entry is undefined: today ELSEWHERE holds only `epics-rerun/spine.md` and `epics-no-boundary/spine.md`, and no plan in phase 8 adds this one. The test pushes `samples/readiness/prd.md: stamped, but no parent found`, and `node --test tests/samples.test.mjs` fails after Task 1 and still after Task 2. Every existing sample folder that holds a prd.md (top level, epics-split, spine-from-prd, spine-job, spine-outside-input, spine-rerun, spine-conventions) also holds a brief.md, so nothing in the repo covers this case. The fix is an entry `'readiness/prd.md': 'brief.md'` in ELSEWHERE, with tests/samples.test.mjs added to Task 1's Files. The plan's own Context line 36 states that pattern but never applies it to the PRD.

entries.claim: The `ends-on-already-built` spec contradicts itself. It requires the last two non-blank lines to be the command and then the sentence, and it allows a closing fence only after the sentence. So the one likely fenced output, the command in its own fence with the already-built sentence as prose after it, fails a correct run. `ends-on-named-command` (line 111) inherits the same pattern.
entries.failure_scenario: Plan 3 has SKILL.md show the lead-in, the command and the already-built sentence each in its own fenced block. A model that fences the shell command after the lead-in `To hand this design to Cadence, run:` ends with the lines "```", "/cad-phase add --brief .planning/seldon", "```" and "If Cadence has already built this design, there's nothing to hand off.". The last two non-blank lines are then the closing fence and the sentence, not the command and the sentence. A regex built as written (command line, blanks, sentence, optional trailing fence, end) misses, and `handoff-cadence` and `handoff-named` score below 1.00 on correct D-14/D-15 output. That uses up tries from the three-try budget. The only fenced form the spec allows puts the prose sentence inside the same code fence as the command, which is the unlikely one. The D-21 checks in Verify (2) are all negative inputs, so nothing before the live run shows the correct fenced form passing.

entries.claim: Task 3 says its outcome is D-10's fix "with the finding carried" and that its graders, D-21 checks, run and stale check prove it, but none of them checks that the crossing finding reached spine.md. D-10 is locked and explicitly rejects "a rerun with no finding carried". No grader looks at spine.md's content for a `Kind: boundaries` decision between Loans and Repairs.
entries.failure_scenario: Seed samples/readiness/ (the spine has no decision on repairs, and Plan 4 Verify (3) checks `grep -ci repair` prints 0). Replay the one-finding history, then send `/seldon fix them`. Suppose the spine rerun ignores the finding line and only rewords an existing decision, for example adding repairs to S-06's sentence, or adds a decision of another kind. It still makes an Edit to spine.md, so edits-spine passes. It doesn't touch epics.md, so no-epics-write and no-epics-edit pass. It ends on the spine confirm question, so ends-on-confirm passes. Any byte change to spine.md also makes `--stale` print `stale: epics.md was built from an earlier spine.md`, so Verify (5) passes. readiness-fix scores 1.00, yet the next readiness check reports E-02's crossing again, which is the loop D-10 rejects. A file-target regex grader on .planning/seldon/spine.md would catch this, in the form of stale-epics' stamps-spine-hash, requiring a `Kind: boundaries` decision that mentions repairs.

entries.claim: Nothing in this plan proves that the agent, run over samples/readiness/, returns exactly the one E-02 crossing line that the readiness-fix and readiness-hand-off histories replay. That leaves D-19's rule unchecked: a replayed history must be a transcript the skill at HEAD can produce. Task 1 stops testing on the claim that "Task 2's history pins the one-finding report", but that history is written by hand, and Task 2 Verify (2) only checks it against SKILL.md's text forms.
entries.failure_scenario: Plan 4 Task 1's testing scope hands this proof to Plan 6 ("Plan 6's runs prove the agent reads it that way"). Yet Plan 6's live agent runs seed only readiness-uncovered (readiness-findings) and the clean samples (readiness-agent), and readiness-fix and readiness-hand-off are replays. Suppose a real bare /seldon over samples/brief.md plus samples/readiness/ also prints a `Decision left open:` line, for example about checkout depending on the repair log, or prints no crossing at all. Then both histories record a turn the skill never produces, contrary to D-19, and every case still scores 1.00. The other plans as written include no run that would expose this, Plan 7's full suite among them.

entries.claim: The retry path runs evals that Plan 1's recorded SECURITY approval doesn't cover, and the plan's SECURITY gate only checks whether full runs are covered, so those runs start without a SECURITY stop. Plan 1 (Context, 'Runs covered') covers only the per-case runs in Plans 3, 5 and 6, plus Plan 7's full-suite runs, and it allows a second full run only when a case in the first missed on model variance. Plan 7 adds two kinds of run beyond that. After a ruled fix to SKILL.md or the agent, it reruns the affected cases solo, which are per-case runs in Plan 7, and then makes a 'next full run' that is a second full run not caused by model variance.
entries.failure_scenario: First full run: readiness-fix misses because of SKILL.md's text. Daneel rules on a fix, the executor lands it and reruns readiness-fix solo with `--case`. The plan's gate ('If none is recorded, or the recorded one doesn't cover full runs, stop at a checkpoint marked SECURITY') passes, because full runs are covered, so the solo run starts with no SECURITY checkpoint. The executor then makes a second full run. Plan 1's approval allows that only after a variance miss. Two kinds of run go outside D-04's fail-closed terms, and the plan never sets a limit on solo tries in Plan 7 (Plan 1's limit is three tries per case).

entries.claim: Task 3 has the executor write one README line per new case 'saying what the case gives Seldon and what it checks', and rewrite resume-later's line, but its Reads list none of the case files. It lists README.md#Evals, .github/workflows/test.yml and phase 7's PLAN-8, not the seven new cases' case.yaml or graders and not evals/resume-later/.
entries.failure_scenario: An executor that follows Reads writes the seven lines from this plan's prose instead of the graders. A line then claims a check the case doesn't grade, or misses one it does. For example, handoff-named grades `/cad-phase add --brief .planning/seldon/repair-log` plus the already-built sentence, and readiness-not-run grades the not-checked line coming before the lead-in. Verify (1) only compares names, so a wrong description passes every check in Task 3.

entries.claim: Plan 4 stamps `samples/readiness/prd.md` with `samples/brief.md`'s hash, but no plan adds a `readiness/prd.md` entry to `ELSEWHERE` in `tests/samples.test.mjs`. Task 1 does not list that test file in its Files, and Task 2 adds only `readiness-uncovered/epics.md`. So the samples test that Plan 4 pins, and that Plans 7 and CI run, fails.
entries.failure_scenario: `stampProblems()` (tests/samples.test.mjs:34-37) looks for the parent as a sibling, `samples/readiness/brief.md`. That file does not exist, and `ELSEWHERE['readiness/prd.md']` is undefined, so the test reports `samples/readiness/prd.md: stamped, but no parent found`. Plan 4 Task 1 Verify (2), Task 2 Verify (2), and Plan 7's unit suite under the coverage gate (AC6) all fail.
